{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, the passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same story.", "text": "Then Grandma lowered the apron, and her face did something Mara had not seen it do in three years. It crumpled and bloomed at the same time, like a paper flower dropped in water.

"Elijah Thomas," she said, her voice cracking on every syllable. "You didn't write."

"I know, Gran."

"Not once since Christmas."

"I know." He stopped at the foot of the steps, suddenly looking younger, like the boy who used to track mud across her clean kitchen floor and stand waiting to be scolded. "I'm sorry."

She came down the last step and took his face in both her hands, turning it toward the porch light as if checking for damage. Her thumbs brushed a pale scar along his jaw that Mara hadn't noticed. Grandma's mouth tightened, but she didn't ask. Not yet.

"You're thin," she said instead.

"You say that every time."

"Because it's true every time." She pulled him down into a hug, and Eli had to stoop nearly in half. Over her shoulder, his eyes found Mara's, bright and wet, and he gave her a helpless little shrug.

The pickup's engine ticked as it cooled. Somewhere past the cornfield, a whip-poor-will started up its endless question.

"Well," Grandma said at last, stepping back and wiping her eyes briskly, all business again. "There's pot roast keeping warm, and it's been keeping warm since six o'clock. Get your bag."

Eli glanced back at the truck, and something passed over his face, quick and shadowed.

"About that," he said. "I didn't come alone.""}
